issues.description: Method return type mismatch for Stock.take(String): the problem statement UML (problem_statement.md) declares Stock.take(String) to return an int (using -1 to indicate failure). The solution implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java) defines take(String) returning int. However, the template implementation (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java) defines take(String) returning boolean. This inconsistency will confuse students and can cause compilation errors or incorrect logic when they implement SealSaloon or follow the UML (e.g., callers expecting -1/remaining quantity vs. true/false).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template with the UML/problem statement and the solution: change the template's Stock.take(String) signature to return int and implement it to return -1 when the ingredient does not exist or is out of stock, otherwise decrement the quantity and return the remaining quantity. Concretely, update template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java: change 'public boolean take(String ingredient)' to 'public int take(String ingredient)' and adjust return values to use -1 for failure and remaining quantity on success. Alternatively, if the intended API is boolean, update the problem statement and solution consistently to use boolean, but prefer aligning the template to the UML/solution to avoid blocking students.
